instruction: Set up a Thunderbird filter to mark all emails from 'noreply@automated.com' as junk automatically. Configure this locally in Thunderbird only.

metadata.explanation: Task requires creating a filter to classify emails as junk. The evaluator verifies an enabled filter with 'Mark as Junk' action exists.
metadata.verification: Evaluator checks Thunderbird filter configuration file for expected filter rules with appropriate action and enabled status.

llm_judge_reasons: Complete verification coverage: Evaluator checks all instruction requirements - enabled status, action type, and filter condition
Expected rules correctly specify enabled='yes', action='Mark as Junk', and condition pattern matching via regex
Condition verification uses regex pattern '.*from.*noreply@automated\.com.*' which correctly matches filter conditions targeting the specified email address
Metric function _match_record_with_regex (lines 27-36) properly handles regex matching for the condition field
The condition field is parsed as a list and joined for regex matching (lines 31-34), which aligns with Thunderbird filter file format
Logic flow is correct: getter extracts msgFilterRules.dat file -> metric parses filter entries -> regex match validates condition contains 'from' and 'noreply@automated.com'
